newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of PPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady ahead of PPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in lacklustre trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. May producer price index (PPI) and April business inventories data, dealers said on Friday.
The U.S. producer price index for May is forecast to show a gain of 0.1 percent compared with a 0.6 percent decline reported in April.
April business inventories are expected to show a gain of 0.2 percent against March's 0.3 percent increase.

"Rates were steady to a little bit softer in the morning on some position adjustments. Some people are waiting for tonight's release of the producer price index and business inventories figures, for more clues to market direction," a dealer said.
"The numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions for the weekend, so I don't think there will be much impact," he said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend, Monday/Tuesday and week-fixed eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, respectively.
Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from Thursday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent and three-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 percent.
Nine-months eased 1/16 percentage point to 6 5-7/8 percent and twelve-months eased 1/16 point to 6-1/8 6 percent.
